input.rationale: The filed probe came back and it decides the boundary question, so this turn interprets that receipt for the child question and corrects the parent account where the receipt contradicts it. All four comparisons resolved with complete witnesses. The controls hold: the leader's heartbeat left the follower's reported leader at 1 (index 59 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624) and the up-to-date candidate's pre-vote under that live lease produced no response at all (index 60). The decision comparison is violated: the same MsgForgetLeader type, delivered with From=3 (a real voter), To=2 and Term=2 (the follower's own current term, so no field is illegal), returned no step error and moved the reported leader from 1 to 0 (index 61). The consequence comparison is violated too: the identical pre-vote that the lease had just withheld was granted immediately afterwards (index 62). So the acceptance does not depend on the term field being unset, and the term-less form that every earlier receipt used was the weaker case rather than the load-bearing one. The parent rationale said the opposite as mechanism - that because the wire form carries no term field Step treats it as a local message and skips term checks - which now reads as if the unset term were what makes the message act; that clause is corrected there to the actual mechanism, that the term fails to gate the message at all (no equality case in the term switch, no case for the type in the type switch, so control lands in stepFollower, which clears r.lead without reading the term), and the parent now cites this receipt for that point. Two knowledge entries record the new observation and the general dispatch mechanism. No further experiment is filed this turn: the remaining run budget is under one turn, and an uninterpreted execution is worse than a closed question.

knowledge.statement: A peer-form MsgForgetLeader carrying a well-formed term acts exactly like the term-less form. With three real RawNodes (voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, equal logs at index=10/term=1) and follower 2 holding a live leader context at term 2, delivering MsgForgetLeader with From=3, To=2 and Term=2 through RawNode.Step returned no error and set SoftState.Lead from 1 to 0 (index 61 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624); the identical pre-vote from the up-to-date candidate that the lease had withheld immediately before was granted immediately after (index 62), while the leader's real heartbeat had left Lead at 1 (index 59) and the same pre-vote under that live lease had produced no response at all (index 60).
knowledge.conditions: Follower is a voter holding a live leader context at the same term as the delivered message; sender is a real voter; Config.CheckQuorum and PreVote set; ReadOnlyOption is not ReadOnlyLeaseBased; the message is handed to RawNode.Step directly.

knowledge.statement: Step's term switch has cases only for a zero term, a higher term and a lower term, so a message whose term equals the receiver's own passes the whole term switch untouched and reaches the switch on its type; MsgForgetLeader has no case there either, so control lands in the default dispatch r.step(r, m), which for a follower is stepFollower, where the type sets r.lead = None whenever a leader is recorded and refuses only under ReadOnlyLeaseBased. The leader context is therefore cleared at the term the follower already holds, with no term comparison and no error, so the acceptance is a property of the missing classification rather than of the term field.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a follower; message type MsgForgetLeader; message term equals the receiver's own term or is zero; sender id is not checked for membership; ReadOnlyOption != ReadOnlyLeaseBased.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered no, and the receipt answers it with all four comparisons complete and no missing indices, so the acceptance is not an artefact of the unset term. Both controls hold in the same stream: the leader's real heartbeat left the follower's reported leader at 1 (index 59), which is the context the forged message has to leave alone, and the candidate's real pre-vote, delivered under that live lease, produced no response at all (index 60), which excludes the reading that this follower grants pre-votes regardless of its leader. The decision comparison is then violated in the way that matters: MsgForgetLeader with From=3, To=2 and Term=2 - a real voter as sender and the follower's own current term, so no field is illegal - was accepted with an empty step error and moved the reported leader from 1 to 0 (index 61). The consequence comparison is violated as well: the identical pre-vote that had just been withheld was granted after that message (index 62), so the support change follows the well-formed form exactly as it follows the term-less one. Mechanism, from the sources: Step's term switch matches only a zero term, a higher term and a lower term, so a message whose term equals the receiver's own passes the whole switch untouched; MsgForgetLeader has no case in the type switch either, so control reaches the default dispatch that calls stepFollower, where the type clears r.lead whenever one is recorded and only refuses under ReadOnlyLeaseBased. The term field therefore does not gate the message, and the earlier term-less receipts were the weaker instance of a gap that stands with a legal message. Scope and open items: this remains a message no correct peer constructs, so the sender is byzantine or buggy; a higher-than-own term was not measured and would additionally move the receiver's term; the follower was a voter holding a live leader context, and the no-leader case is the weaker one; and the receipt measures the follower's answer to one pre-vote rather than re-running the full election, which the sibling quorum receipt covers.
counterevidence: The message is still one that no code path in the snapshot produces for the network, so this remains a byzantine or faulty peer rather than a correct one exerting influence; the receipt removes the dependence on an illegal field, it does not supply a legitimate sender.
The acceptance is not unconditional: stepFollower refuses the type outright when ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which was not the configuration under test here.
limitations: Single process with hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration and one term value (the follower's own term 2); a message carrying a higher term was not measured and would additionally advance the receiver's term.
The measured consequence is the follower's answer to one pre-vote, not a completed election; the forged-election path is bounded separately in the sibling quorum receipt.
The follower under test is a voter with a live leader context; the case where it has no leader at all is not distinguished here and is the weaker case.

interpretations.rationale: Current account across eight receipts, one of which is a repeat that reproduced the same experiment identically. A MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted with no error through both documented inbound paths - RawNode.Step (index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7, reproduced at 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a) and the real Node interface that applications use, where the node's own reported leader went 1 -> 0 and the same transition was produced by the intended local API Node.ForgetLeader (indices 42 and 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40, with the local-type control holding at 41). It changes the support a follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease is granted after the accepted message, the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (indices 14, 15 and 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; index 25 of the latest). The window per message is closed by the next genuine leader message (heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick, index 7, and the same pre-vote was ignored again, index 8), but a sender repeating the message each round keeps it open without any repair failing: three consecutive rounds restored the context and granted again (indices 32, 35, 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849, whose repair comparisons hold at 33 and 36). The harm stays bounded: after the forged election the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a), so no committed entry was lost. Cause and controls are unchanged, with one correction the newest receipt forces: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although only the local ForgetLeader APIs produce it, and the term field is not what gates the message. Step's term switch matches only a zero, a higher and a lower term, so a non-zero term equal to the receiver's own falls straight through to the type switch and its default dispatch into stepFollower, where the type clears r.lead without reading the term; a receipt delivered exactly that well-formed form - From=3, a real voter, and Term=2, the follower's own term - and it returned no error, moved Lead 1 -> 0 and had the initially withheld pre-vote granted immediately afterwards (indices 61 and 62 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624, with the heartbeat and under-lease controls holding at 59 and 60). So the term-less form used by the earlier receipts was the weaker case rather than the load-bearing one, and the missing classification is sufficient on its own; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected or ignored in every receipt. Conditions the effect depends on, stated explicitly: the defeated lease test exists only when Config.CheckQuorum is set (inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout), so the marginal effect of the forged message is specific to CheckQuorum deployments; the type is a no-op on leaders, so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term; and a candidate whose log is behind is still refused by isUpToDate, so the message does not manufacture support for stale candidates. The exposure this creates is now measured rather than only bounded by reading: an elected leader that afterwards hears from nobody is already a follower at its first CheckQuorum check, with its term unchanged, and stays a follower at the next sample (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512), so the overlap between the incumbent and the forged leader lasts one election timeout of the incumbent's own clock in the silent case. Remaining limits are scope: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the message outright, and the persistence loop using an exact one-message-per-tick cadence. The repeat of this very experiment from its retained inputs in a clean copy returned the same twelve comparison outcomes with the same witness indices (under-lease controls holding at 3, 4, 7 and 10; the peer-form message accepted at 5 and 13; the same pre-vote granted afterwards at 6 and 14; the vote granted at 15; the candidate leading at term 3 at 17; the repair heartbeat and the ignored pre-vote after it at 7 and 8), which is what makes the account schedule-stable rather than the product of one favourable interleaving. The later boundary receipt is a single execution rather than a repeat, so it extends the account's scope by one well-formed message form without inheriting that reproduction evidence.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that followers grant pre-votes and votes regardless of their leader is excluded by the under-lease control in every receipt, including the control round inside the persistence loop, the Node-interface control, and the two controls of the boundary receipt (indices 59 and 60 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624).

The reading that the finding only fires because the delivered message left its term field unset - and so collapses into the separately refuted term-zero path - is now excluded by the well-formed delivery, which cleared the leader context with a legal term (index 61 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624).
The change is per-message and reversible: the context returns with the next real leader heartbeat in every round, so this is not a stuck state and does not survive a sender that stops.
The widest severity reading is excluded by the aftermath receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver a protobuf message of any type - including one the module only produces locally - to the documented inbound path, repeatedly; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test, and the well-formed receipt shows the message needs no illegal field to be accepted.

Single-process, hand-delivered messages: no wall-clock duration, jitter, packet loss, authentication or multi-host transport behaviour is measured, and the persistence loop used an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.
The quorum-scale election uses one voter plus the candidate, and it was re-executed identically in the repeat, so its outcome is reproduced even though the quorum size itself was not varied.

The incumbent's overlap with the new leader is bounded and measured for the silent case - one election timeout of its own clock with an unchanged term (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512) - but that bound does not follow when the leader still hears from some voters, or when CheckQuorum is disabled.
The effect requires CheckQuorum to be enabled for the lease test it defeats, and it is a follower-side change only (leaders ignore the type).

Reproduction: the principal experiment was executed twice from its fixed inputs in clean copies and both runs produced identical comparison outcomes and witness indices; the boundary receipt that removes the dependence on the unset term was executed once, and messages carrying a higher term were not measured at all.

It does not supply or replace this account's reproducibility evidence, which remains the repeat 3f8d0a1b83304e5c9032b909703bb1c4 of this interpretation's own experiment.

knowledge.statement: IsLocalMsg returns true only for MsgHup, MsgBeat, MsgUnreachable, MsgSnapStatus, MsgCheckQuorum, MsgStorageAppend, MsgStorageAppendResp, MsgStorageApply and MsgStorageApplyResp; MsgForgetLeader (MessageType 23) is therefore classified as a network message, and RawNode.Step rejects a message only when IsLocalMsg(m.Type) && !IsLocalMsgTarget(m.From), returning ErrStepLocalMsg otherwise delivering it to raft.Step.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot; classification is by MessageType only, independent of From/To and of any term field; node.Step has the same predicate and silently ignores local types received from a non-local sender.

knowledge.statement: No code path in the snapshot sends, forwards or replicates MsgForgetLeader: its only producers are RawNode.ForgetLeader and node.ForgetLeader, which call raft.Step directly, and stepFollower acts on it locally by setting r.lead=None (refusing when ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlyLeaseBased); a message with Term==0 is classified as a local message by Step and skips all term comparisons.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot; grep over the whole tree shows MsgForgetLeader only in rawnode.go, node.go, raftpb (enum/aliases), rafttest handlers and no r.send/message-construction site.

knowledge.statement: In Step, a MsgVote or MsgPreVote with a higher term is ignored (no response at all) when force is false and inLease holds, where inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout; a follower that has lead==None fails inLease and instead evaluates canVote, where the third clause (m.Type == MsgPreVote && m.Term > r.Term) holds for a pre-vote from any node, so an up-to-date candidate is granted.

knowledge.statement: Both intended producers of MsgForgetLeader bypass the inbound filter rather than depending on it: RawNode.ForgetLeader calls raft.Step directly, and node.ForgetLeader uses the internal step path that sends the message to the receive channel instead of Node.Step. Classifying MsgForgetLeader as a local message would therefore leave both APIs working (their messages never pass IsLocalMsg) while making RawNode.Step return ErrStepLocalMsg and Node.Step ignore messages of that type received from a peer.

knowledge.statement: MsgForgetLeader is the only message type in the enum whose producers are purely local and yet is absent from isLocalMsg. Sweeping the enum against the filter and producer sites: MsgHup, MsgBeat, MsgCheckQuorum, MsgUnreachable, MsgSnapStatus, MsgStorageAppend, MsgStorageAppendResp, MsgStorageApply and MsgStorageApplyResp are all locally produced and all listed; MsgProp, MsgApp, MsgAppResp, MsgVote, MsgVoteResp, MsgSnap, MsgHeartbeat, MsgHeartbeatResp, MsgTransferLeader, MsgTimeoutNow, MsgReadIndex, MsgReadIndexResp, MsgPreVote and MsgPreVoteResp are produced for or forwarded over the network and correctly unlisted; MsgForgetLeader is produced only by the two local ForgetLeader APIs and is unlisted, so it is the single exception.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution is claimed): the enum in raftpb, the isLocalMsg array in util.go, and every construction site for MsgForgetLeader found by searching the tree (rawnode.go, node.go, and the rafttest handlers, none of which put it on the wire). This bounds the earlier finding: the omission is a single-point classification gap, not a pattern.

knowledge.statement: A leader that stops hearing from a quorum steps down by itself: tickHeartbeat fires a MsgCheckQuorum step every election timeout when Config.CheckQuorum is set, and stepLeader responds to MsgCheckQuorum by calling ProgressTracker.QuorumActive (which treats each non-learner's RecentActive flag, reset for every peer but itself after each check, as a vote) and becoming a follower when that quorum is not active. So in a CheckQuorum deployment the coexistence of the incumbent and a leader elected at a higher term is bounded by an election timeout of the incumbent's own logical clock, not by how long the new leader's messages take to arrive.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution is claimed): raft.go 862-880 (tickHeartbeat's election-timeout branch dispatching MsgCheckQuorum), raft.go 1281-1294 (stepLeader's MsgCheckQuorum arm stepping down and clearing RecentActive for every peer but itself) and tracker/tracker.go 205-218 (QuorumActive over the voters' RecentActive flags) (set true on any peer message, cleared for all peers but the leader at each check). Applies only when Config.CheckQuorum is enabled; the bound was not measured in any receipt of this run, so it constrains the earlier receipts' scope rather than being witnessed by them.

knowledge.statement: A MsgReadIndex received by a leader that has not committed an entry in its own term is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and answered only through releasePendingReadIndexMessages, which is called from a single site - the leader's append-response path once commit progress releases the queue - and which first requires committedEntryInCurrentTerm, otherwise it logs an error and leaves the queue intact. No other code path writes or clears the field: the search over the tree finds only the field declaration, the queueing site and that helper with its one call site, so a request queued before the node loses leadership is never cancelled; it is answered only if the same node again becomes leader and commits in a later term, in which case it is answered with the commit index reached at release time, and it otherwise stays unanswered.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): field declaration raft.go 428-435, queueing at raft.go 1361-1368, the release helper at raft.go 2127-2143 and its single call at raft.go 1548-1556. The caller contract that makes the unanswered case acceptable is node.go 218-224 (ReadIndex: 'request can be lost without notice, therefore it is user's job to ensure read index retries'). Not a defect finding; recorded because it bounds what the module guarantees about completion of an accepted read duty, and because a caller that assumed otherwise would retry unnecessarily - or not at all.

knowledge.statement: A read request queued by a leader that has no commit in its own term is not answered while that node loses leadership: after its own quorum check demoted it to follower at its old term, no read state had appeared for the request it still owed, and nothing answered it while it was not leader. When the same node led again at a higher term and committed an entry there, the stale request was released with the read index committed at that release time (12, where the index recorded at acceptance was 10) and with the request context it was accepted with.

knowledge.statement: The regression is transient and self-healing. MaybeDecrTo's non-replicate branch lowers Next to max(min(rejected, matchHint+1), Match+1) and clears MsgAppFlowPaused, but while the progress is in StateSnapshot (a) the reject path in stepLeader calls BecomeProbe only for StateReplicate, so the state is unchanged, and (b) sendAppend returns immediately because IsPaused is true for StateSnapshot, so nothing is sent from the regressed value. Both ways out of StateSnapshot recompute Next from PendingSnapshot: a MsgSnapStatus without a rejection calls BecomeProbe with Next = max(Match+1, PendingSnapshot+1), and one with a rejection first zeroes PendingSnapshot and then calls BecomeProbe with Next = Match+1. So a stale rejection in that state at most logs a decrement, and the snapshot outcome restores a consistent Next; no probe from the wrong index and no stall follows.

knowledge.statement: The application-facing ordering duties are enforced by fatal guards, not by clamping: appending entries whose predecessor is below the commit index panics, committing to an index past the last index panics, reporting an applied index outside [previously applied, committed] panics, accepting application for an index past committed panics, and computing a non-positive application size budget panics. The only tolerated adjustments are non-fatal: applied-to bookkeeping clamps its outstanding-size counter at zero, and application is paused (applyingEntsPaused) once the outstanding size reaches the configured limit, resuming when the application's acknowledgement, via Applied or the storage apply response, brings the outstanding size down. Entry rewriting above the commit index is allowed by design, which is how a follower replaces a divergent uncommitted tail.

knowledge.statement: Step skips all term handling for a message whose term is zero, treating it as a local message, and then dispatches on its type: for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap that reaches stepFollower, which sets the election timer to zero and adopts m.From as the leader before handling the payload. So term-zero trust is not specific to MsgForgetLeader; what is specific to it is that it is the only locally-produced type missing from the inbound filter, so it reaches that trust from a peer with no illegal field at all, while a peer would have to send MsgApp or MsgHeartbeat with an illegal zero term to reach the same state change. That illegal-term path is not a correct-peer behaviour, its effect is bounded (a follower's advertised leader and timer, with a divergent uncommitted tail that the next real leader truncates) and it needs no classification change to be described.

interpretations.rationale: The current account rests on read source plus a native construction probe (not yet a retained receipt). Remaining scope limits: a single inbound message affects one node, the election still needs a quorum of grants, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses the change entirely (so lease-based reads are protected), and the next leader message restores r.lead. Registered gap: the length of that window and whether a quorum can be reached inside it. interpretations.rationale: The question is answered with all four comparisons holding. While the node owed the request but was not leader, no read state was produced for it (index 52) and the demotion happened at the term the node had led at (same index), so it was the module's own quorum check rather than a peer's higher term that ended the leadership; the request therefore waited through the demotion unanswered. Once the same node led again at term 3 and committed at index 12, the stale request was released with read index 12 and with the context it was accepted with (index 54, both comparisons), so the late answer is attributable to that request and is not stale - it reports an index at least as new as the one recorded when the request was accepted. Nothing here is a defect: the module neither answers a request it cannot justify nor answers one with an outdated index, and the only gap is the one the interface documentation already permits, namely a request that is never answered at all if the node that owes it never leads again.
counterevidence: A read state appearing for the request while the node was a follower would have refuted the source reading; none appeared.
limitations: Two voters were contacted at most, so quorum was exactly the leader plus one follower; the same path with a different quorum size is not measured.
The case where the node never leads again is unobservable beyond the source fact that no other code path can answer the request.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered, and the answered half is now measured rather than only read. With the leader elected but nothing committed in its term, the ReadIndex request produces no read state at all (index 48), which is the queueing behaviour the sources predicted; the follower's acknowledgement of that term's entry then moves the leader's commit index to 11 with a quorum of matches (index 49); and the released read state carries read index 11 together with the exact request context that was issued (index 50 for both the index and the identity comparison), so the answer is attributable to that request and is at least as new as the moment it was accepted. The remaining half of the question - a request queued by a leader that then loses leadership before committing - is now measured too: after the leader's own quorum check demoted it (StateFollower at term 2, its term unchanged, and no read state for the request it still owed, index 52), the node led again at term 3, committed at index 12, and the stale request was released there with read index 12 and the original context (index 54, both comparisons), so the late answer is attributable and not stale. The source reading's expectations were: nothing clears the queue on a term change and the release helper is reachable only from a leader path, so such a request is answered only if the same node leads again and commits, and otherwise is never answered, which the interface documentation permits by telling callers that read requests can be lost and retries are their job. Nothing here is a defect, and the finding that matters for the main account is unchanged. What used to rest on reading alone is now bounded by a receipt: nothing clears the queue on a term change, so a request owed by a demoted leader waits through the demotion, is not answered while that node is not leader, and is answered only if the same node leads again and commits - with the index reached at that later release.
counterevidence: The unanswered case is permitted by the same snapshot's ReadIndex documentation, so it cannot be scored as a defect without importing a stronger requirement than the module states.
The answered case is safe rather than merely successful: the released index is the commit index at release time, which is at least as new as the index recorded when the request was accepted.
limitations: Both halves are now measured: the completing path in one receipt and the leadership-loss path in another; what remains unmeasured is the case where the same node never leads again, which is unobservable by construction beyond the observation that no other code path can answer it, and the retry behaviour of applications.

interpretations.rationale: Current account across seven receipts, one of which is a repeat that reproduced the same experiment identically. A MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted with no error through both documented inbound paths - RawNode.Step (index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7, reproduced at 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a) and the real Node interface that applications use, where the node's own reported leader went 1 -> 0 and the same transition was produced by the intended local API Node.ForgetLeader (indices 42 and 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40, with the local-type control holding at 41). It changes the support a follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease is granted after the accepted message, the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (indices 14, 15 and 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; index 25 of the latest). The window per message is closed by the next genuine leader message (heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick, index 7, and the same pre-vote was ignored again, index 8), but a sender repeating the message each round keeps it open without any repair failing: three consecutive rounds restored the context and granted again (indices 32, 35, 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849, whose repair comparisons hold at 33 and 36). The harm stays bounded: after the forged election the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a), so no committed entry was lost. Cause and controls are unchanged: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although only the local ForgetLeader APIs produce it, and because the wire form carries no term field Step treats it as a local message and skips term checks; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected or ignored in every receipt. Conditions the effect depends on, stated explicitly: the defeated lease test exists only when Config.CheckQuorum is set (inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout), so the marginal effect of the forged message is specific to CheckQuorum deployments; the type is a no-op on leaders, so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term; and a candidate whose log is behind is still refused by isUpToDate, so the message does not manufacture support for stale candidates. The exposure this creates is now measured rather than only bounded by reading: an elected leader that afterwards hears from nobody is already a follower at its first CheckQuorum check, with its term unchanged, and stays a follower at the next sample (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512), so the overlap between the incumbent and the forged leader lasts one election timeout of the incumbent's own clock in the silent case. Remaining limits are scope: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the message outright, and the persistence loop using an exact one-message-per-tick cadence. The repeat of this very experiment from its retained inputs in a clean copy returned the same twelve comparison outcomes with the same witness indices (under-lease controls holding at 3, 4, 7 and 10; the peer-form message accepted at 5 and 13; the same pre-vote granted afterwards at 6 and 14; the vote granted at 15; the candidate leading at term 3 at 17; the repair heartbeat and the ignored pre-vote after it at 7 and 8), which is what makes the account schedule-stable rather than the product of one favourable interleaving.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that followers grant pre-votes and votes regardless of their leader is excluded by the under-lease control in every receipt, including the control round inside the persistence loop and the Node-interface control.
The change is per-message and reversible: the context returns with the next real leader heartbeat in every round, so this is not a stuck state and does not survive a sender that stops.
The widest severity reading is excluded by the aftermath receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver a protobuf message of any type - including one the module only produces locally - to the documented inbound path, repeatedly; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test.

Single-process, hand-delivered messages: no wall-clock duration, jitter, packet loss, authentication or multi-host transport behaviour is measured, and the persistence loop used an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.

interpretations.rationale: The suspicion is defeated by the surrounding state machine, and the mechanism is worth stating because it is what makes the counter regression harmless. The trigger is reachable - a rejection for an append sent before the snapshot satisfies Next-1 == rejected in StateSnapshot - and MaybeDecrTo does lower Next there, so the counter can be inconsistent with PendingSnapshot for a while. What prevents that from mattering is the pair of protections around it: the reject path upgrades to probing only from StateReplicate, so the state stays snapshot; IsPaused is unconditionally true in that state, so the sendAppend that follows is a no-op and no probe is issued from the regressed value; and both exits recompute Next from PendingSnapshot rather than from the regressed value (success keeps PendingSnapshot, failure zeroes it first, and either way BecomeProbe derives Next from Match and PendingSnapshot). The consequent replication therefore resumes from a correct index in both outcomes, which is the property the audit asks about. Nothing here is a defect, and no execution was needed: the state that would have to persist for a defect does not, and each step of that claim is a cited branch.
counterevidence: The counter regression itself is real and observable in the debug log line the reject path prints, so the account does not claim the value never moves; it claims the value cannot be used before it is recomputed.
limitations: Source reading only: no execution exercised the interleaving in this run, and the claim rests on the four cited branches rather than on a receipt.
The trigger assumes an append sent before the snapshot can still be rejected afterwards; that ordering is allowed by the message model but was not produced here.
A change to IsPaused or to either exit from StateSnapshot would invalidate this reading, so the two protections are cited explicitly for a reviewer to re-check.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered from the sources and the answer is a design fact rather than a defect. Each ordering violation an application could commit - rewriting committed entries, committing past the last index, applying out of order or past committed, or accepting application past committed - reaches a guard that panics, so the bookkeeping cannot be quietly advanced or rewound by a misreporting client; the two tolerated cases are treated differently on purpose (the outstanding-size counter saturates at zero, and further application pauses until the client acknowledges progress). Two consequences matter for reading this run's evidence: first, the module's before/after style observations are meaningful because the counters it reports cannot have been silently clamped into place; second, a client that misreports brings down its own process rather than corrupting the state machine, so the guards protect the module and the peer set without pretending to validate the application. Rewriting entries above the commit index is deliberately not a violation, which is exactly how a follower truncates a divergent uncommitted tail.
counterevidence: One guard can also fire on values the module computes itself (the application size budget), which would indicate an internal inconsistency rather than client misbehaviour; the account therefore does not claim every panic implies a faulty client.
limitations: Source reading only: no execution triggered a guard in this run, so the account rests on the cited branches rather than on a receipt.
Whether an application receives a distinguishable error before the fatal path is not established here; the guards are panics, and the API returns errors only for proposal-related rejections.

interpretations.rationale: Both comparisons resolved. Control: the leader's real heartbeat set follower 2's reported leader to 1 (index 56), so the follower's context was live and the admission event records it as a follower at term 2 with no leader before that. Boundary: the same type from node 3 with no term field was accepted with no error and moved the reported leader to 3 (index 57), so the predicate that a message carrying no term must not change the leader context is contradicted. What this means for the main finding is settled: the classification gap is not the only way a peer can reach the lead-setting branch, since any network type with an unset term gets there as well, which is why the finding is framed as a classification omission (with a legal, need-nothing-extra field) rather than as the general absence of input validation. What is not settled is whether that second path is itself a defect: the module's convention is that a message with term zero is a local message, and it documents no duty to validate the term field of network types, so the claim would require a duty the snapshot does not state. Consequences and limits: adopting a peer as leader misdirects that follower's forwarded proposals and resets its election timer, but the log itself self-heals because the next genuine leader's message carries a higher term and truncates the divergent tail above the commit index, and no commit can be advanced on the follower's word alone.
counterevidence: A correct peer never produces an unset term on a network type, so no crash-fault schedule reaches this path; it requires a byzantine or buggy sender, which is outside the CFT fault model the audit prioritises.
The variant where the follower has no current leader is not distinguished here, and the probe used one where a live leader existed, which is the stronger case.
limitations: Single process with hand-delivered messages and one configuration; no receipt exists for the proposal-misdirection consequence, which is argued from the branch that sets lead rather than observed.

The judgment is left unresolved rather than refuted: a source statement assigning term validation to the module, or a documented caller duty to never deliver term-less messages, would settle it either way.
Nothing here changes the main account's witnesses, which rest on a message that needs no illegal field at all.

interpretations.rationale: The observation stands and the judgment is now settled against a defect. Control and boundary both resolved: the leader's real heartbeat set follower 2's reported leader to 1 (index 56), and the same type from node 3 with no term field was accepted with no error and moved it to 3 (index 57), so the predicate that a message carrying no term must not change the leader context is contradicted. The defect claim is refuted on three sourced grounds, checked in the contract context rather than assumed: Step is documented only as advancing the state machine with a given message, on both the Node and RawNode interfaces, with no duty to validate the term field; doc.go documents that MsgProp is deliberately term-less because the send path overwrites its term, which shows an unset term is a marker for local or forwarded traffic rather than an error signal; and the path requires a sender that emits a network type with the field unset, which no correct peer does, so no crash-fault schedule reaches it and the module assumes peer correctness as Raft does. Consequences and limits are unchanged: a follower that adopts a peer on this basis misdirects its forwarded proposals and resets its election timer, the log self-heals on the next genuine leader message because that message carries a higher term and truncates the divergent tail, and nothing here alters the main finding, whose message needs no illegal field at all and whose duty the module does state through its own inbound filter.
counterevidence: The strongest argument the other way is that the module accepts a message whose sender is not a member and whose term is unset, both of which a hardened implementation could check; the snapshot's contract does not require either check, which is why this is recorded as a boundary rather than a second finding.
The proposal-misdirection consequence is argued from the branch that sets lead, not observed in a receipt.
limitations: Single process with hand-delivered messages and one configuration; no receipt covers the misdirection consequence.
Refutation rests on the absence of a stated duty plus the documented term-less MsgProp; a future source statement assigning term validation to the module would reopen it.
How a transport should treat term-less messages is outside this module and outside the captured snapshot.

result.summary: The filed probe returned a decisive receipt and this turn interprets it and corrects the parent account. CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624 resolved all four comparisons with complete witnesses: the heartbeat control left follower 2's reported leader at 1 (index 59), the up-to-date candidate's pre-vote under that live lease produced no response at all (index 60), and then the peer-form MsgForgetLeader with From=3, To=2 and Term=2 — a real voter and a well-formed term, so no field illegal — was accepted with an empty step error and moved the reported leader from 1 to 0 (index 61), after which the identical pre-vote that the lease had just withheld was granted (index 62). The answer to the boundary question is therefore no: the acceptance is not an artefact of the unset term, and every earlier receipt used the weaker message form. Mechanism, from source: Step's term switch matches only zero, higher and lower terms, so an equal non-zero term passes it untouched, and MsgForgetLeader has no case in the type switch either, so control reaches the default dispatch into stepFollower, which clears r.lead without reading the term. What changed in the records: (1) a new interpretation for the child question @legal_term_inbound, conclusion violated, defect_claim asserted, citing indices 59-62; (2) the parent interpretation (ce33f7b508af4244883ac9c81a2a4696-question-0) was corrected where its rationale said the acceptance worked because the wire form carries no term field and Step treats it as a local message — that causal clause now states that the term fails to gate the message at all, cites the new receipt for it, records index 46 alongside 45, and no longer implies the finding needs an illegal field; a joint-history note explains why a receipt from a separate producer experiment (the child's) is admissible evidence for the parent; (3) two knowledge entries, one fact capturing the well-formed delivery and one behavior capturing the term-switch fall-through into stepFollower. No new experiment was filed: remaining run budget is under one turn, and leaving an uninterpreted execution would be worse than closing this question cleanly. Update validated: valid=true, execution_requested=false.

knowledge.statement: IsLocalMsg returns true only for MsgHup, MsgBeat, MsgUnreachable, MsgSnapStatus, MsgCheckQuorum, MsgStorageAppend, MsgStorageAppendResp, MsgStorageApply and MsgStorageApplyResp; MsgForgetLeader (MessageType 23) is therefore classified as a network message, and RawNode.Step rejects a message only when IsLocalMsg(m.Type) && !IsLocalMsgTarget(m.From), returning ErrStepLocalMsg otherwise delivering it to raft.Step.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot; classification is by MessageType only, independent of From/To and of any term field; node.Step has the same predicate and silently ignores local types received from a non-local sender.

knowledge.statement: No code path in the snapshot sends, forwards or replicates MsgForgetLeader: its only producers are RawNode.ForgetLeader and node.ForgetLeader, which call raft.Step directly, and stepFollower acts on it locally by setting r.lead=None (refusing when ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlyLeaseBased); a message with Term==0 is classified as a local message by Step and skips all term comparisons.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot; grep over the whole tree shows MsgForgetLeader only in rawnode.go, node.go, raftpb (enum/aliases), rafttest handlers and no r.send/message-construction site.

knowledge.statement: In Step, a MsgVote or MsgPreVote with a higher term is ignored (no response at all) when force is false and inLease holds, where inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout; a follower that has lead==None fails inLease and instead evaluates canVote, where the third clause (m.Type == MsgPreVote && m.Term > r.Term) holds for a pre-vote from any node, so an up-to-date candidate is granted.

knowledge.statement: A MsgReadIndex received by a leader that has not committed an entry in its own term is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and answered only through releasePendingReadIndexMessages, which is called from a single site - the leader's append-response path once commit progress releases the queue - and which first requires committedEntryInCurrentTerm, otherwise it logs an error and leaves the queue intact. No other code path writes or clears the field: the search over the tree finds only the field declaration, the queueing site and that helper with its one call site, so a request queued before the node loses leadership is never cancelled; it is answered only if the same node again becomes leader and commits in a later term, in which case it is answered with the commit index reached at release time, and it otherwise stays unanswered.

knowledge.statement: The regression is transient and self-healing. MaybeDecrTo's non-replicate branch lowers Next to max(min(rejected, matchHint+1), Match+1) and clears MsgAppFlowPaused, but while the progress is in StateSnapshot (a) the reject path in stepLeader calls BecomeProbe only for StateReplicate, so the state is unchanged, and (b) sendAppend returns immediately because IsPaused is true for StateSnapshot, so nothing is sent from the regressed value. Both ways out of StateSnapshot recompute Next from PendingSnapshot: a MsgSnapStatus without a rejection calls BecomeProbe with Next = max(Match+1, PendingSnapshot+1), and one with a rejection first zeroes PendingSnapshot and then calls BecomeProbe with Next = Match+1. So a stale rejection in that state at most logs a decrement, and the snapshot outcome restores a consistent Next; no probe from the wrong index and no stall follows.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): MaybeDecrTo at tracker/progress.go 226-261, BecomeProbe at 130-152, IsPaused at 262-278, the reject path at raft.go 1505-1520 and MsgSnapStatus handling at 1611-1624. The reachable trigger is a rejection for an append the leader sent before entering StateSnapshot, which under this source is the only way MaybeDecrTo sees rejected == Next-1 there.

knowledge.statement: The application-facing ordering duties are enforced by fatal guards, not by clamping: appending entries whose predecessor is below the commit index panics, committing to an index past the last index panics, reporting an applied index outside [previously applied, committed] panics, accepting application for an index past committed panics, and computing a non-positive application size budget panics. The only tolerated adjustments are non-fatal: applied-to bookkeeping clamps its outstanding-size counter at zero, and application is paused (applyingEntsPaused) once the outstanding size reaches the configured limit, resuming when the application's acknowledgement, via Applied or the storage apply response, brings the outstanding size down. Entry rewriting above the commit index is allowed by design, which is how a follower replaces a divergent uncommitted tail.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): log.go 136-140 (append guard), 322-328 (commitTo guard), 330-341 (appliedTo guard and counter clamp), 344-356 (acceptApplying guard and the pause condition), 234-238 (budget guard), with the client duties stated in node.go around ReadIndex/Ready and in the Ready struct documentation. The guards fire on values the module itself passes (from Ready/Advance) as well as on values an application reports in MsgStorageApplyResp, so a misreporting application is the party that trips them.

knowledge.statement: Step skips all term handling for a message whose term is zero, treating it as a local message, and then dispatches on its type: for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap that reaches stepFollower, which sets the election timer to zero and adopts m.From as the leader before handling the payload. So term-zero trust is not specific to MsgForgetLeader; what is specific to it is that it is the only locally-produced type missing from the inbound filter, so it reaches that trust from a peer with no illegal field at all, while a peer would have to send MsgApp or MsgHeartbeat with an illegal zero term to reach the same state change. That illegal-term path is not a correct-peer behaviour, its effect is bounded (a follower's advertised leader and timer, with a divergent uncommitted tail that the next real leader truncates) and it needs no classification change to be described.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): raft.go 1094-1100 (the term switch whose first case is the local-message case) and 1730-1739 (stepFollower setting electionElapsed and lead for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap). The contrast assumes a follower already at a term of at least 1, which every node reaches through becomeFollower(1, None) before it can lead or vote; the finding it clarifies is the main question's, whose evidence is the receipts cited there.

knowledge.statement: Step's term switch has cases only for a zero term, a higher term and a lower term, so a message whose term equals the receiver's own passes the whole term switch untouched and reaches the switch on its type; MsgForgetLeader has no case there either, so control lands in the default dispatch r.step(r, m), which for a follower is stepFollower, where the type sets r.lead = None whenever a leader is recorded and refuses only under ReadOnlyLeaseBased. The leader context is therefore cleared at the term the follower already holds, with no term comparison and no error, so the acceptance is a property of the missing classification rather than of the term field.

interpretations.rationale: The current account rests on read source plus a native construction probe (not yet a retained receipt). MsgForgetLeader is generated only by the local ForgetLeader API, is never put on the wire by any code path in the snapshot, and stepFollower implements it as a local authority-state change (r.lead = None). The module's own inbound filter exists precisely to stop locally-generated types from being delivered from peers, but the type is missing from isLocalMsg, so RawNode.Step accepts it and, because its term field is absent (0), Step treats it as a local message and skips term checks; stepFollower then clears r.lead. With CheckQuorum+PreVote that removal of the leader context disables the lease test that otherwise suppresses support for a candidate whose log is already up to date, so an unauthenticated peer message converts the follower from 'silent' to 'grant' for the same pre-vote request. The retained suite does not contradict this: TestIsLocalMsg/TestIsResponseMsg enumerate every other MessageType but not MsgForgetLeader, and the interaction tests call RawNode.ForgetLeader directly, so neither covers the classification. Remaining scope limits: a single inbound message affects one node, the election still needs a quorum of grants, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses the change entirely (so lease-based reads are protected), and the next leader message restores r.lead. Registered gap: the length of that window and whether a quorum can be reached inside it. The requested experiment supplies the discriminating comparison set and its receipt must be read before the account is treated as execution-backed.
limitations: No retained receipt yet: the mechanism is established by source reading and by a native probe in a scratch copy whose output is not a controller receipt.

Fault-model assumption stated in the experiment scope: a peer may construct and deliver any protobuf message type over the unauthenticated raft transport; the library's inbound filter, not the transport, is the protection.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased configurations refuse MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so this does not by itself break lease-based reads.

One delivered message clears one node's leader context; a new leader still needs a quorum of granted votes, so the consequence is bounded disruption (loss of the intended 'quorum must agree the leader is dead' condition), not log divergence.

interpretations.rationale: The retained execution confirms the sourced suspicion. Comparison 2 (acceptance predicate) has a valid witness at index 4: a message of the type only the local ForgetLeader API produces, sent by peer 3 in wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field), is accepted by RawNode.Step with no error, and the follower's Lead drops from 1 to 0. Comparison 3 (consequence) has a valid witness at index 5: the same real MsgPreVote from an up-to-date candidate that produced no response while the lease held (control, comparison 1, holds at index 3) is answered with MsgPreVoteResp Reject=false once the leader context has been cleared. Comparison 0 holds at index 2, so the inbound filter itself works for a type that is classified local (MsgCheckQuorum from the same sender returns ErrStepLocalMsg and leaves Lead=1): the gap is specific to MsgForgetLeader's absence from isLocalMsg, which reading of util.go and the retained (equally incomplete) TestIsLocalMsg list already indicated. Because the forged message carries no term field, Step treats it as a local message and skips all term comparisons, so no term or sender check stands in for the missing classification. Consequences that remain scoped: exactly one node's leader context is cleared per delivered message and the election still needs a quorum of grants, the next genuine leader message restores r.lead, and ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses MsgForgetLeader outright, so lease-based reads are not broken. The mechanism is therefore a real authority/context-validity defect with bounded disruption impact: it defeats the intended 'a quorum must agree the leader is dead' condition that the ForgetLeader API documents, using a message the module's own inbound contract is supposed to reject. What is still unexecuted is registered as a child question: how long the window stays open in ticks and whether forged deliveries to a quorum yield a second leader at a higher term while the incumbent still reports leadership.

ce33f7b508af4244883ac9c81a2a4696-gap-0.explanation: Partially answered from the receipt plus source: the window is not closed by the forgery itself, so it lasts from the accepted message until the next genuine leader message is processed (stepFollower sets r.lead=m.From for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap), i.e. at most one heartbeat interval per follower; the run shows the same pre-vote changing from ignored (index 3) to granted (index 5) across the accepted message, but no ticks were advanced and no quorum was involved, so neither the tick bound nor quorum-wide election was measured.

counterevidence: Comparison 4 (local-API control) evaluated as unknown, with the diagnostic 'Ambiguous prerequisite association; missing lease.node' plus 'Missing operation admission fields or identity' for the heartbeat event: its identity field was 'node' while its admission alias was the heartbeat prerequisite, which carries no 'node' field. That is a defect in my comparison specification, not target behaviour, so the correlated observation of the local API clearing lead on a follower with lead_before=1 (event index 1) is preserved here as an uncorrelated observation and is not counted as a witness.

The observation is single-node: no evidence in this receipt shows a quorum-wide effect or a second leader, and the retained interaction expectations (testdata/forget_leader*.txt) show the intended local-API behaviour, so nothing here contradicts the designed local path.
limitations: The decisive inbound message is constructed by the harness in peer wire form; it is within the stated fault-model assumption that a peer may deliver any protobuf message type to the public inbound path of RawNode.Step/node.Step, since raft's wire format and the module's own filter (not the transport) are the boundaries in scope.

interpretations.rationale: Current answer to the question, with the receipt folded in: a MsgForgetLeader arriving from a peer through RawNode.Step does reach the follower state machine, is accepted without error, clears its live leader context (Lead 1 -> 0), and does change the support it gives an up-to-date candidate's pre-vote while the leader is still alive: the identical pre-vote is ignored under the lease and granted afterwards. The cause is that the message type is missing from isLocalMsg even though the only producers of MsgForgetLeader are the local ForgetLeader APIs, and because the wire form has no term field Step classifies it as a local message and performs no term check. Controls in the same receipt hold: a genuinely local type from the same sender is rejected (ErrStepLocalMsg) and the under-lease pre-vote is not granted, so neither 'the filter is broken in general' nor 'pre-votes are always granted' explains the witnesses. Scope limits stand: one node per message, the next leader message restores the context, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses the change, and the quorum-scale consequence plus the tick-length of the window are recorded in the open child question rather than claimed here.

ce33f7b508af4244883ac9c81a2a4696-gap-0.explanation: See the receipt-backed account above and the experiment-level interpretation: the window closes on the next genuine leader message (at most one heartbeat interval per follower), which the executed run did not advance ticks for, and no quorum-scale election was executed.

interpretations.rationale: Current account with both receipts folded in. A MsgForgetLeader sent by a peer in wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) reaches the follower state machine through RawNode.Step, is accepted with no error, and clears the live leader context (Lead 1 -> 0) - witnessed first at index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 and reproduced at index 5 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568. It changes the support the follower gives an up-to-date candidate's pre-vote: the identical request that produced no response while the lease held (under-lease controls at indices 3/4 of the first receipt and 4/10 of the second) is granted afterwards (indices 5 of the first, 6/14 of the second). The second receipt extends that to the cluster level: one such message to the other voter was enough for the follower to grant the real vote (index 15) and for the candidate to become StateLeader at term 3 (index 17) while the incumbent still reported StateLeader at term 2 (index 18), i.e. a healthy leader is replaced without the quorum-wide external evidence the ForgetLeader contract requires; the window opened per follower is closed by the next genuine leader message (indices 7/8), and the local API still produces the same state change legitimately (index 2), which is exactly why the inbound path must not. Cause and controls are unchanged from the first account: the type is absent from isLocalMsg even though its only producers are the local ForgetLeader APIs and, with no term field, Step treats it as a local message and performs no term check; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected (indices 2 first / 3 second). Scope limits stand: one delivered message clears one follower's context, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses the change, the deposit of the incumbent depends on the new leader's messages reaching it (child question @forged_forget_aftermath), and no entry loss or log divergence was observed, so this is a disruption/authority-transition defect rather than an integrity defect.

ce33f7b508af4244883ac9c81a2a4696-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568: the window lasts until the next genuine leader message (restoring heartbeat at index 7, identical pre-vote ignored again at index 8, one leader tick with HeartbeatTick=1), and a quorum-scale election did follow the forged delivery (granted pre-vote index 14, granted vote index 15, candidate StateLeader at term 3 index 17 while the incumbent still reported leadership at term 2 at index 18).

counterevidence: The strongest competing explanation for the grants - that this follower grants pre-votes and votes to any up-to-date candidate regardless of the leader - is excluded by the under-lease controls in both receipts (no response at all while the context was intact).

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered from the sources and the answer is a design fact rather than a defect. Each ordering violation an application could commit - rewriting committed entries, committing past the last index, applying out of order or past committed, or accepting application past committed - reaches a guard that panics, so the bookkeeping cannot be quietly advanced or rewound by a misreporting client; the two tolerated cases are treated differently on purpose (the outstanding-size counter saturates at zero, and further application pauses until the client acknowledges progress). Two consequences matter for reading this run's evidence: first, the module's before/after style observations are meaningful because the counters it reports cannot have been silently clamped into place; second, a client that misreports brings down its own process rather than corrupting the state machine, so the guards protect the module and the peer set without pretending to validate the application. Rewriting entries above the commit index is deliberately not a violation, which is exactly how a follower truncates a divergent uncommitted tail.

limitations: Source reading only: no execution triggered a guard in this run, so the account rests on the cited branches rather than on a receipt.

interpretations.rationale: Both comparisons resolved. Boundary: the same type from node 3 with no term field was accepted with no error and moved the reported leader to 3 (index 57), so the predicate that a message carrying no term must not change the leader context is contradicted. What this means for the main finding is settled: the classification gap is not the only way a peer can reach the lead-setting branch, since any network type with an unset term gets there as well, which is why the finding is framed as a classification omission (with a legal, need-nothing-extra field) rather than as the general absence of input validation. What is not settled is whether that second path is itself a defect: the module's convention is that a message with term zero is a local message, and it documents no duty to validate the term field of network types, so the claim would require a duty the snapshot does not state. Consequences and limits: adopting a peer as leader misdirects that follower's forwarded proposals and resets its election timer, but the log itself self-heals because the next genuine leader's message carries a higher term and truncates the divergent tail above the commit index, and no commit can be advanced on the follower's word alone.

Control and boundary both resolved: the leader's real heartbeat set follower 2's reported leader to 1 (index 56), and the same type from node 3 with no term field was accepted with no error and moved it to 3 (index 57), so the predicate that a message carrying no term must not change the leader context is contradicted. The defect claim is refuted on three sourced grounds, checked in the contract context rather than assumed: Step is documented only as advancing the state machine with a given message, on both the Node and RawNode interfaces, with no duty to validate the term field; doc.go documents that MsgProp is deliberately term-less because the send path overwrites its term, which shows an unset term is a marker for local or forwarded traffic rather than an error signal; and the path requires a sender that emits a network type with the field unset, which no correct peer does, so no crash-fault schedule reaches it and the module assumes peer correctness as Raft does. Consequences and limits are unchanged: a follower that adopts a peer on this basis misdirects its forwarded proposals and resets its election timer, the log self-heals on the next genuine leader message because that message carries a higher term and truncates the divergent tail, and nothing here alters the main finding, whose message needs no illegal field at all and whose duty the module does state through its own inbound filter.
counterevidence: The strongest argument the other way is that the module accepts a message whose sender is not a member and whose term is unset, both of which a hardened implementation could check; the snapshot's contract does not require either check, which is why this is recorded as a boundary rather than a second finding.
The proposal-misdirection consequence is argued from the branch that sets lead, not observed in a receipt.
limitations: Single process with hand-delivered messages and one configuration; no receipt covers the misdirection consequence.
Refutation rests on the absence of a stated duty plus the documented term-less MsgProp; a future source statement assigning term validation to the module would reopen it.
How a transport should treat term-less messages is outside this module and outside the captured snapshot.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered no, and the receipt answers it with all four comparisons complete and no missing indices, so the acceptance is not an artefact of the unset term. Both controls hold in the same stream: the leader's real heartbeat left the follower's reported leader at 1 (index 59), which is the context the forged message has to leave alone, and the candidate's real pre-vote, delivered under that live lease, produced no response at all (index 60), which excludes the reading that this follower grants pre-votes regardless of its leader. The decision comparison is then violated in the way that matters: MsgForgetLeader with From=3, To=2 and Term=2 - a real voter as sender and the follower's own current term, so no field is illegal - was accepted with an empty step error and moved the reported leader from 1 to 0 (index 61). The consequence comparison is violated as well: the identical pre-vote that had just been withheld was granted after that message (index 62), so the support change follows the well-formed form exactly as it follows the term-less one. Mechanism, from the sources: Step's term switch matches only a zero term, a higher term and a lower term, so a message whose term equals the receiver's own passes the whole switch untouched; MsgForgetLeader has no case in the type switch either, so control reaches the default dispatch that calls stepFollower, where the type clears r.lead whenever one is recorded and only refuses under ReadOnlyLeaseBased. The term field therefore does not gate the message, and the earlier term-less receipts were the weaker instance of a gap that stands with a legal message. Scope and open items: this remains a message no correct peer constructs, so the sender is byzantine or buggy; a higher-than-own term was not measured and would additionally move the receiver's term; the follower was a voter holding a live leader context, and the no-leader case is the weaker one; and the receipt measures the follower's answer to one pre-vote rather than re-running the full election, which the sibling quorum receipt covers.
counterevidence: The message is still one that no code path in the snapshot produces for the network, so this remains a byzantine or faulty peer rather than a correct one exerting influence; the receipt removes the dependence on an illegal field, it does not supply a legitimate sender.
The acceptance is not unconditional: stepFollower refuses the type outright when ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which was not the configuration under test here.
limitations: Single process with hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration and one term value (the follower's own term 2); a message carrying a higher term was not measured and would additionally advance the receiver's term.
The measured consequence is the follower's answer to one pre-vote, not a completed election; the forged-election path is bounded separately in the sibling quorum receipt.
The follower under test is a voter with a live leader context; the case where it has no leader at all is not distinguished here and is the weaker case.

interpretations.rationale: Current account across eight receipts, one of which is a repeat that reproduced the same experiment identically. A MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted with no error through both documented inbound paths - RawNode.Step (index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7, reproduced at 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a) and the real Node interface that applications use, where the node's own reported leader went 1 -> 0 and the same transition was produced by the intended local API Node.ForgetLeader (indices 42 and 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40, with the local-type control holding at 41). It changes the support a follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease is granted after the accepted message, the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (indices 14, 15 and 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; index 25 of the latest). The window per message is closed by the next genuine leader message (heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick, index 7, and the same pre-vote was ignored again, index 8), but a sender repeating the message each round keeps it open without any repair failing: three consecutive rounds restored the context and granted again (indices 32, 35, 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849, whose repair comparisons hold at 33 and 36). The harm stays bounded: after the forged election the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a), so no committed entry was lost. Cause and controls are unchanged, with one correction the newest receipt forces: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although only the local ForgetLeader APIs produce it, and the term field is not what gates the message. Step's term switch matches only a zero, a higher and a lower term, so a non-zero term equal to the receiver's own falls straight through to the type switch and its default dispatch into stepFollower, where the type clears r.lead without reading the term; a receipt delivered exactly that well-formed form - From=3, a real voter, and Term=2, the follower's own term - and it returned no error, moved Lead 1 -> 0 and had the initially withheld pre-vote granted immediately afterwards (indices 61 and 62 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624, with the heartbeat and under-lease controls holding at 59 and 60). So the term-less form used by the earlier receipts was the weaker case rather than the load-bearing one, and the missing classification is sufficient on its own; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected or ignored in every receipt. Conditions the effect depends on, stated explicitly: the defeated lease test exists only when Config.CheckQuorum is set (inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout), so the marginal effect of the forged message is specific to CheckQuorum deployments; the type is a no-op on leaders, so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term; and a candidate whose log is behind is still refused by isUpToDate, so the message does not manufacture support for stale candidates. The exposure this creates is now measured rather than only bounded by reading: an elected leader that afterwards hears from nobody is already a follower at its first CheckQuorum check, with its term unchanged, and stays a follower at the next sample (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512), so the overlap between the incumbent and the forged leader lasts one election timeout of the incumbent's own clock in the silent case. Remaining limits are scope: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the message outright, and the persistence loop using an exact one-message-per-tick cadence. The repeat of this very experiment from its retained inputs in a clean copy returned the same twelve comparison outcomes with the same witness indices (under-lease controls holding at 3, 4, 7 and 10; the peer-form message accepted at 5 and 13; the same pre-vote granted afterwards at 6 and 14; the vote granted at 15; the candidate leading at term 3 at 17; the repair heartbeat and the ignored pre-vote after it at 7 and 8), which is what makes the account schedule-stable rather than the product of one favourable interleaving. The later boundary receipt is a single execution rather than a repeat, so it extends the account's scope by one well-formed message form without inheriting that reproduction evidence.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that followers grant pre-votes and votes regardless of their leader is excluded by the under-lease control in every receipt, including the control round inside the persistence loop, the Node-interface control, and the two controls of the boundary receipt (indices 59 and 60 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624).

The reading that the finding only fires because the delivered message left its term field unset - and so collapses into the separately refuted term-zero path - is now excluded by the well-formed delivery, which cleared the leader context with a legal term (index 61 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624).
The change is per-message and reversible: the context returns with the next real leader heartbeat in every round, so this is not a stuck state and does not survive a sender that stops.
The widest severity reading is excluded by the aftermath receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver a protobuf message of any type - including one the module only produces locally - to the documented inbound path, repeatedly; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test, and the well-formed receipt shows the message needs no illegal field to be accepted.

Single-process, hand-delivered messages: no wall-clock duration, jitter, packet loss, authentication or multi-host transport behaviour is measured, and the persistence loop used an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.
The quorum-scale election uses one voter plus the candidate, and it was re-executed identically in the repeat, so its outcome is reproduced even though the quorum size itself was not varied.

The incumbent's overlap with the new leader is bounded and measured for the silent case - one election timeout of its own clock with an unchanged term (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512) - but that bound does not follow when the leader still hears from some voters, or when CheckQuorum is disabled.
The effect requires CheckQuorum to be enabled for the lease test it defeats, and it is a follower-side change only (leaders ignore the type).

Reproduction: the principal experiment was executed twice from its fixed inputs in clean copies and both runs produced identical comparison outcomes and witness indices; the boundary receipt that removes the dependence on the unset term was executed once, and messages carrying a higher term were not measured at all.
